title: Getting Started with a Simple HTML Document
objectives: Create a minimal valid HTML document
Understand the role of the DOCTYPE, html, head and body elements
Open an HTML file in a browser and view the result

sections.title: What is an HTML document?
sections.content: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard language used to create web pages. An HTML document is simply a text file that contains special tags. The browser reads those tags and turns them into the page you see.

sections.title: The smallest useful HTML page
sections.content: Every modern HTML page should start with a DOCTYPE declaration and contain an <html> element that wraps a <head> and a <body>. The head holds metadata (title, character encoding, links to CSS). The body holds the visible content.

sections.title: Working example
sections.code:
Hello, World!

This is my first HTML document.
explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> tells the browser to use standards mode (HTML5).
<html lang="en"> is the root element; lang helps accessibility and search engines.
<head> contains information about the document, not visible content.
<meta charset="UTF-8"> ensures special characters display correctly.
<title> appears in the browser tab and is used by search engines.

items.why: The browser may switch to quirks mode and layout can break.
Content in the head is not rendered as page content.
items.fix: Move paragraphs, headings and images into <body>

sections.title: Guided practice
steps: Create a new file named index.html
Type the DOCTYPE and the basic skeleton shown above
Change the title to your name
Add a second paragraph about yourself
Open the file in a browser (double-click or use Live Server)

questions.q: Which element contains the visible content of the page?
questions.explain: The <body> element holds everything the user sees on the page.

options: Tells the browser to use HTML5 standards mode
questions.explain: It instructs the browser to render the page in standards mode using the HTML5 rules.

points: An HTML document is a text file with tags that the browser interprets.
The minimal structure is DOCTYPE → html → head + body.
Always include charset and a meaningful title.
Visible content belongs only in the body.
